fold_split_leakage.finding: No temporal overlap between folds — each fold is an independent CPUBacktestEngine with its own data slice. Trades from fold-1 cannot carry into fold-2 because engines don't share state.

cur_score_fix_32a2f49.finding: Fix correctly sets cur_score = min(init_fold_scores) and hist[0]['score'] = cur_score, ensuring the improvement threshold (local_best[0] > cur_score + min_improve) compares fold-min against fold-min on the same scale. Both baseline and all subsequent comparisons use the fold-min scale. Test test_baseline_cur_score_uses_min_fold_in_walk_forward correctly demonstrates the fix (baseline full-val=400/min-fold=100, candidate full-val=200/min-fold=150 → accepted).

walk_forward_criterion.finding: Inner loop computes selection_score = min(fold_scores_local) and compares via min across folds. This is the worst-case selection strategy as specified. Confirmed at rb_governor.py:860-862.

tail_holdout_usage.finding: Tail holdout engine is scored ONLY at lines 888-895 AFTER the entire search loop completes. It is never consulted during TP/SL/capital grid search. No overfitting to tail data is possible.

n_splits_1_with_tail.finding: n_splits=1 + RB_RISK_GRID_USE_TAIL_HOLDOUT=True correctly builds 1 fold engine + 1 tail engine, but use_walk_forward evaluates to False (len(fold_engines)==1). The fold engine is unused for scoring; the tail engine is used for the final report only. This is correct but has no dedicated test.

small_data_duplication.finding: _make_walk_forward_fold_engines duplicates data 3x when a symbol has < n_splits+1 rows (line ~737). The duplicated rows create identical data across folds, defeating walk-forward independence for tiny per-symbol data. The test test_small_data_does_not_crash only checks crash-safety, not fold independence. In practice, val_selection symbols should have hundreds of rows, so this is an unlikely edge case. Consider adding a warning log and a test asserting fold data independence.

fold_engine_memory.finding: Each fold engine creates a full CPUBacktestEngine with a copied, prepared DataFrame. With 2 folds + 1 tail + existing train + valid = ~5x val_selection memory. val_selection is a subset of full data, so acceptable. Confirmed.

risk_grid_cost.finding: Walk-forward evaluates every TP/SL/capital combo on each fold. For 8x5x4=160 combos, 2 folds, 2 passes: 640 fold evaluations (matches spec estimate of ~1920 extra total evaluations including initial baseline). No caching of fold scores across passes — each pass re-evaluates. Acceptable for the grid size.

redundant_training_backtests.finding: Each fold evaluation calls _evaluate_ruleset(train_engine, fold_engine, trial), which re-runs train_engine.simulate_rule_set(trial) producing the same result as the main evaluation. ~640 redundant training simulations (160 combos × 2 folds × 2 passes). Not a correctness issue; fits within the spec's cost estimate. Consider caching train_m per-combo in the future.

memory_footprint.finding: Each fold engine holds a full DataFrame copy. With 2 folds + 1 tail + train + valid ≈ 5 copies of val_selection data. Acceptable since val_selection is a subset. No memory leak detected — engines are garbage-collected when _optimize_risk returns.

two_fold_overfit_test.finding: test_rejects_overfit_combo correctly demonstrates that 2-fold walk-forward picks combo C (min=340) over combo A (min=-100) and combo B (min=200), even though combo A has the highest single-fold score (400). Legacy mode picks combo A. Assertion validates selected_combo == (2.5, 1.5, 20.0). Test is robust and well-constructed.

high_fix_test.finding: test_baseline_cur_score_uses_min_fold_in_walk_forward exercises the production code path directly. Sets up baseline full-val=400/min-fold=100, candidate full-val=200/min-fold=150. Asserts (1) candidate is accepted (combo 2.5,1.2,20.0), (2) hist[0]['score'] == 100.0 (not 400). Without the fix, 150 > 400+0.01 would fail. Test correctly validates the fix.

tail_holdout_tests.finding: test_tail_fields_appear_in_final_history_entry checks ONLY the final history entry (hist[-1]) for tail fields — correct. test_no_tail_fields_when_tail_engine_none checks ALL entries lack tail fields — correct. Both use monkeypatch to control _evaluate_ruleset and verify specific tail metric values (2.5% return, 1.3 PF, 3.0% DD).

regression_test.finding: test_regression_single_fold_no_tail passes fold_engines=None, tail_holdout_engine=None and asserts no fold_scores or min_fold_score in any history entry. This is a structural regression test (checks absence of new fields), not a bit-identical output test. The implementation achieves effective bit-identical behavior by passing fold_engines=None when wf_splits<=1 and not use_tail, and the _optimize_risk function treats None as legacy path. The _is_positive_good call was refactored (config lookups moved outside inner loop) but since they're simple getattr calls with no side effects, behavior is preserved.

test_coverage_gaps.finding: No test for n_splits=1 + tail_holdout=True (code path works but untested). No test for fold data independence with small data (only crash-safety tested). No test for n_splits > 2 (spec says n_splits>=2 generality but only n_splits=2 tested).

audit_linkage.finding: 4 grep matches for 'audit finding #3|audit finding #12' in rb_governor.py — 2 at _make_walk_forward_fold_engines header, 2 at caller site in run_rb_governor_pipeline. All are greppable.

function_naming.finding: _make_walk_forward_fold_engines is well-named (verb_noun pattern), single-purpose (split data + build engines), and has clear docstring explaining per-symbol chronological split convention and return type.

optimize_risk_signature.finding: Generalized signature adds fold_engines and tail_holdout_engine as optional params with None defaults. Backward compatible — existing callers pass no new args. Type hints are correct (list[CPUBacktestEngine] | None). The local_best tuple grew from 4 to 5 elements with correct type annotation. Readable and well-structured.

config_flags.finding: RB_RISK_GRID_WF_SPLITS=2 (default) with clear docstring: '1 = legacy single-fold', plus audit citation. RB_RISK_GRID_USE_TAIL_HOLDOUT=True (default) with clear docstring: 'reported but NOT used during search', plus audit citation. PHASE4_TAIL_HOLDOUT_FRACTION comment updated to mention RB Governor. All defaults are sensible.

findings.title: Small-data duplication fallback defeats walk-forward independence
findings.description: When a symbol has fewer than n_splits+1 rows, the code duplicates data 3x via pd.concat([sym_df] * (n_splits+1)). This causes the same data points to appear in both fold-1 and fold-2, eliminating the walk-forward benefit. The test test_small_data_does_not_crash only verifies crash-safety, not fold independence. In practice, production val_selection symbols should have hundreds of rows, making this rare. However, if any symbol in scoring_val has very few rows (e.g., late-added symbol with minimal history), the walk-forward folds become non-independent without any warning.
findings.recommendation: Add a warning log when the duplication fallback is triggered (logger.warning with symbol name and row count). Optionally add a test that constructs 2 symbols — one with enough rows and one with <n_splits+1 rows — and asserts the small symbol's data is NOT identical across folds (or that a warning is emitted).

findings.title: Redundant training backtests in walk-forward inner loop
findings.description: Each call to _evaluate_ruleset(train_engine, fold_engine, trial) re-runs train_engine.simulate_rule_set(trial), producing the same train_m as the outer _evaluate_ruleset call for the same combo. With 160 combos x 2 folds x 2 passes = 640 redundant training simulations. The outer train_m is correctly reused in _is_positive_good checks, but the simulation itself is still executed inside _evaluate_ruleset.
findings.recommendation: Future optimization: extract train_m from the outer evaluation and pass it to a fold-scoring helper that takes the pre-computed train_m. Not needed now — fits within the spec's cost estimate.

findings.title: Missing test coverage for n_splits=1 with tail_holdout=True
findings.description: The configuration n_splits=1 + use_tail=True creates 1 fold engine + 1 tail engine. use_walk_forward is False (len==1) so the fold engine is unused, but the tail engine IS used for final reporting. This code path works correctly but has no explicit test.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that passes n_splits=1, tail_holdout_frac=0.25 and asserts: (1) use_walk_forward is effectively False (no fold_scores in history), (2) tail fields appear in final entry. This would document the intended behavior for this edge configuration.
